purpose: Safe adult-human motion references for image-to-video/avatar reenactment benchmarking and a later two-avatar story.

selection_policy.people: Clearly described adults only; no children or ambiguous ages.
selection_policy.content: Safe everyday actions with bounded motion and no violence or sexual content.
selection_policy.benchmark_clip_seconds: Use one simple 3-5 second action window from each preview; do not ask a generator to reproduce the entire source clip in one pass.
quality_gate: Reject face identity drift, eye/mouth deformation, extra or fused fingers, limb duplication, joint inversion, body/prop interpenetration, temporal flicker, background melting, and action reversal.
Keep camera motion and occlusion low for the first comparison pass.
Compare identity, pose/action, temporal coherence, anatomy, and scene similarity separately.

research_basis.title: Face Consistency Benchmark for GenAI Video
research_basis.use_here: Treat facial identity consistency as its own evaluation dimension rather than hiding it inside a single aesthetic score.

research_basis.title: From Large Angles to Consistent Faces: Identity-Preserving Video Generation via Mixture of Facial Experts
research_basis.use_here: Include both frontal close-ups and pose/view changes because face angle and identity stability fail differently.

research_basis.title: Human Video Generation from a Single Image with 3D Pose and View Control
research_basis.use_here: Score articulated pose, self-occlusion, view alignment, and temporal stability explicitly in human reenactment tests.

continuity_rules: Lock immutable avatar identity references before rendering the story.
Keep wardrobe palettes stable across adjacent shots.
Use one simple primary action per 3-5 second shot.
Render single-avatar shots first; admit dual-avatar shots only after both identities pass independently.

shots.action: At a cafe table, the woman records a short message saying she found a handwritten note.
The man walks through town, notices the message, stops, and looks toward camera.
He walks toward the meeting place, carrying the same small envelope as a continuity prop.
She sees the wrong cafe sign and gestures no, then points off screen toward the correct entrance.
They meet at the cafe table; he passes her the envelope and they compare the note with a phone photo.
They leave together and walk toward the location revealed by the note.
At home they open a small celebration cake box containing the final clue and smile.
shots.gate: Optional ending; reject if utensil, fingers, or cake interaction fails anatomy/temporal QA.
